ogDesc: Northern Thai food, khao soi, nam prik num, makwaen fried chicken, riverside cafés and mountain views — 10 restaurants the locals of Nan keep returning to, with signature dishes, prices, and maps.
eyebrow: Eat like a local in Nan · Updated 2026
intro: Nan is a city where eating well takes zero effort. A few steps into the old town and you're already at khao soi stalls, nam prik num spots, and laab khua joints. Drive up into the mountains toward Bo Kluea and Sapan and you get Northern home cooking plus mountain-view cafés as a bonus. We picked 10 restaurants that locals and visitors talk about most — from Northern Thai spots inside the wiang to hilltop cafés. Signature dishes and locations included, ready to plan meal by meal.
chips: 🍜 Khao soi · Khanom jeen nam ngiao

blocks.html:
What makes Nan special is that it's a small city that takes food seriously. The Northern Thai cooking here isn't tuned for tourists — it's the flavours locals have eaten for generations. Nam prik num with steamed vegetables, pork laab khua loaded with herbs, kaeng kae gai, thick fragrant khao soi, right through to makwaen fried chicken with its distinctive numbing spice that's unique to this region. The old town around Wat Phumin is easy to stroll and graze, and if you want atmosphere there are riverside spots on the Nan River where the breeze is always good. Head out of town toward Bo Kluea and Ban Sapan and local food plus valley-view cafés are waiting in a way you simply won't find anywhere else.

This list features names that genuinely mean something to Nan people. Huen Phuka is one of the most-talked-about Northern Thai restaurants in the city centre — the Nan appetiser platter and makwaen fried chicken are ordered at nearly every table. Huen Chao Nang serves food from the lineage of the old Nan ruling family, right on the river; the Northern-style sour fish curry and nam prik num are the dishes people come back for. Huen Hom is a small shop, but its khao soi and nam prik have a following. Saneh Nuea is the khao soi and khanom jeen nam ngiao place locals pop into for lunch. Up in the hills you have Boklua View, which serves makwaen fried chicken and local dishes with a valley panorama, and Yudwela Cafe in Ban Sapan — the coffee-with-mountain-view spot everyone heads to. Work through this list and you'll understand exactly why people get hooked on Nan food.

blocks.name: Huen Phuka (HuanPhuka Nan)
blocks.area: Nai Wiang Sub-district, Mueang Nan District, Nan Province
blocks.signature: Nan appetiser platter, pork laab khua, nam prik num, phak chiang da stir-fried with egg, makwaen fried chicken
blocks.descHtml:
If you want one genuine Northern Thai meal in Nan, Huen Phuka is the name locals reach for first. The restaurant sits inside an old wooden house in the Nai Wiang quarter on Kha Luang Road near the city centre — warm, simply decorated in the Lanna style and comfortable. Perfect for a first meal after arriving in Nan, or for a group meal where everyone wants to share many dishes.

The order everyone makes is the Nan appetiser platter — a large sharing plate of nam prik num, sai ua sausage, deep-fried pork skin, steamed vegetables, and boiled egg, one order covers all the flavours. The pork laab khua is made the true Northern way: freshly minced pork and offal stir-fried fragrant with spices, salted and rounded without sourness. The phak chiang da stir-fried with egg is tender with a pleasant bitter edge, and the makwaen fried chicken — its unmistakable numbing-floral aroma from the makwaen spice — is the dish reviewers most often call the standout. Kaeng hang lae and vegetable curries are also solid choices.

Prices are reasonable: most single dishes are in the low-hundred-baht range, the appetiser platter runs around 300 THB and feeds several people. Reviews consistently say you leave full and satisfied with the flavours. Google rating around 4.4, and it consistently ranks among Nan's top Northern Thai restaurants on local food sites — expect a crowd almost every day, especially at lunch and during festivals.

One thing to know: no reservations accepted. If you arrive during peak hours you may wait a little. Arriving outside rush hour or allowing extra time is the move. Open daily 09:00–21:00. Street parking in front. The location is in the old town, so you can walk to temples afterwards with ease.
mustOrder: Phak chiang da stir-fried with egg
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province, group or family dining

blocks.name: Lung Song Noodles
blocks.area: Nai Wiang Sub-district, Mueang Nan District, Nan Province
blocks.signature: Beef/pork noodle soup, clear broth with aromatics, tender marinated meat, yellow egg noodles with beef, dry pork noodles
blocks.descHtml:
Ask a Nan local where to get the best noodles and Lung Song Noodles comes up first, every time. The shop has been part of the city for over fifty years, sitting near the municipal fresh market (the old market) in the old town quarter. The menu is deliberately simple — beef or pork, take your pick — but decades of practice have turned it into a flavour people genuinely miss. Ideal for breakfast through to lunch on a day when you want to eat like a local, not at a polished tourist spot.

The hero is the broth, especially the beef version: a satisfying aroma of beef and herbs that reviewers consistently say needs almost no seasoning added. Top orders are the mixed beef noodle soup and the yellow egg noodles with beef; pork fans usually go for dry thin noodles with pork. The meats are marinated until tender — no chewiness, no sticking. The yellow noodles with meatballs are made in-house and bounce when you bite. The house-made red chilli and vinegar chilli are a detail many regulars mention: sweet-sour, they cut against the broth in a way that makes the flavour feel distinctly this place.

Very affordable — starts around 40 THB, special bowl 50 THB, under 100 THB per person is easy. Opens from around 8 a.m. through to the afternoon, closing around 3 p.m. or when sold out. To avoid queues, come before noon — the midday rush is real. The atmosphere is old-school local, not polished, but the cooking speaks for itself. Easy to reach with reasonable parking around the market area.

Small tip: ordering dry means the broth comes separate, and the flavour will be richer and more intense. Some reviewers find the broth runs slightly salty on its own — add chilli or vinegar gradually since the base already has seasoning. The shop is in a market lane and can be a little hard to spot; dropping a pin on the map first helps.

blocks.name: Huen Chao Nang (Huen Chao Nang)
blocks.area: Tha Lo Sub-district, Phu Phiang District, Nan Province (on the Nan River, adjacent to the city)
blocks.signature: Northern-style sour fish curry (kaeng som mueang), nam prik num with vegetable dips, recipes from the Nan ruling family lineage, no MSG
blocks.descHtml:
Huen Chao Nang (sometimes written as Ruen Chao Nang on some signs) is a riverside Northern Thai restaurant that has anchored itself to the city for nearly twenty years. It sits on the Tha Lo side in Phu Phiang District, a short bridge-cross from the city centre — the same road that leads to Phra That Chae Haeng. The draw here is food from recipes inherited through the Nan ruling family lineage, prepared without MSG, which makes it exactly the right choice for anyone wanting to try genuine old-Nan flavours that are hard to find in ordinary restaurants.

The most talked-about dish is kaeng som mueang pla kang — thick fish in a bracing Northern-style sour curry that multiple reviewers describe as deeply delicious and something they order every single visit. The nam prik num with vegetable dips is more intensely spiced than the standard version — a touch hotter, deeply savoury. For mushroom lovers, the soy-braised shiitake mushrooms are small in appearance but thick in texture, chewy-tender with a good mushroom fragrance that balances the salty sauce. Makwaen fried chicken and pork fried with makwaen are both strong options, as is the full mueang appetiser platter with nam prik, sai ua, pork skin, and steamed vegetables.

The atmosphere is the other selling point: open-air riverside tables with a wide view of the Nan River. Come at dusk and you get a river sunset that many guests call a favourite spot. The restaurant seats over 150, has parking and free Wi-Fi, so it handles large family groups or tour parties easily. Price per person runs roughly 100–200+ THB — fair for the view and quality.

One thing to note: when it's busy, food can come slowly. If you're on a tight schedule, calling ahead to book a riverside table is wise, especially for weekend dinners. Open daily from 11:00 to 21:30 (21:00 on Sundays). When you go, leave time to sit and take in the river — the whole point of Huen Chao Nang is the combination of real local food and the Nan River right in front of you.
mustOrder: Northern-style sour fish curry (kaeng som mueang)
Nam prik num with vegetable dips
blocks.bestFor: Riverside dinner at sunset, family or group dining
blocks.spice: Medium heat (nam prik num is hotter than usual)

blocks.name: Huen Hom (Huen Hom)
blocks.signature: Khao soi chicken/beef, Huen Hom appetiser platter, Huen Hom nam prik, jackfruit salad, makwaen fried chicken
blocks.descHtml:
Huen Hom is a local Northern Thai restaurant in the centre of Nan city, on Suriyaphong Road in Nai Wiang Sub-district, close to the City Pillar Shrine and Wat Ming Mueang — an easy walk from the main tourist zone. The building is an old Lanna-style wooden house assembled from reclaimed timber, old pillars, and a Nan-style roof into an airy pavilion. Inside there are khantoke-style floor seating areas, sala loh, and so suing music playing softly in the background — a relaxed, genuinely local atmosphere for anyone who wants real mueang food in a place that actually feels like Nan.

A favourite starter is the Huen Hom appetiser platter — sai ua, pork skin, nam prik num, and fresh vegetables to open the meal. Follow that with khao soi chicken or beef, Huen Hom nam prik, jackfruit salad, and makwaen fried chicken whose makwaen spice lingers on the tongue. Most reviews praise the food as fresh, distinctly Northern in flavour, and generous for the price — many note that the khao soi and sai ua are the standout dishes.

Price per person around 101–250 THB, reasonable for Northern Thai in the city centre. Open daily from morning through to evening, so you can come for lunch or dinner. Reviews note it gets crowded on weekends and during festivals, with longer waits. Some dishes lean rich — if dining in a group, ordering a spread to share is the way to go.

What keeps this restaurant near the top of visitors' lists in Nan is the combination of a wide spread of local dishes, the old wooden house atmosphere, and a central location — all in one place. The right first stop for anyone who wants to try Northern Thai food in a setting that genuinely smells and feels like Nan.
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province, anyone wanting authentic Northern Thai in a local setting
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: khao soi · Rushen / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 2.0)

blocks.name: Wevari Heritage
blocks.area: On the Nan River, Phu Phiang District side (opposite the old town), Nan Province
blocks.signature: Wevari catfish miang, lemon chicken, basil fried rice, homemade baked goods and coffee, riverside fusion dishes
blocks.descHtml:
For a riverside meal where the breeze never stops, Wevari Heritage is the name that comes up most. The café-bistro sits on the Nan River in Phu Phiang District, across from the old town, close to the bridge and not far from the airport. The décor blends modern with local character — there is both an air-conditioned zone and an open terrace with a full view of the river and the bridge. Good for a relaxed meal with coffee, then sitting and watching the water with nowhere to be.

The menu gets creative with local ingredients. The signature is Wevari catfish miang, named after the restaurant — bold flavours, good for grazing. Popular plates include lemon chicken (sour-spicy-savoury balance), basil fried rice, and garlic pork rice — all straightforward and filling. Those wanting something lighter will find homemade baked goods fresh from the oven plus drinks; coffee fans can try Nan-bean espresso or a chilled peach tea on the riverside terrace.

Prices are accessible — main dishes from 55–200 THB, averaging 100–250 THB per person. Most reviews praise the atmosphere, cleanliness, and the food as being reliably good across the board. Some guests have stayed in Nan for several days and eaten here multiple times. A few reviews note service can slow during busy periods. Allow a little extra time if you're on a schedule. The overall picture is a restaurant people come back to.

Open daily around 08:00–21:00. About four parking spots in front. Located on the Nan River on the Phu Phiang side, opposite the old town, near the bridge — a five-minute drive from the city centre across the bridge. Works for breakfast, lunch, or an afternoon coffee watching the river. If you want a riverside café that also serves a proper meal, this one delivers.
blocks.bestFor: Riverside café crowd, long lazy afternoons

blocks.name: Khao Kриeb Pak Mo (in front of Nan Prison)
blocks.area: Opposite Nan Prison, Phakong Road, Nai Wiang Sub-district, Mueang Nan District, Nan Province
blocks.signature: Khao krиeb pak mo with coconut milk, flavourful filling, thin rice-flour wrapper, served with fresh vegetables (open winter season only)
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Nan during winter and hear locals mention the pak mo cart in front of the prison, know that this is a seasonal treat Nan people wait for all year. The vendor pushes a small wooden cart to the side of Phakong Road, directly opposite Nan Provincial Prison. The operation has run for over twenty-five years and become part of the city's identity. There is one star item: khao krиeb pak mo drizzled with coconut milk — a Nan-specific recipe that sets itself apart by pouring fragrant coconut milk generously over the top. For anyone wanting truly local street food, or families looking to buy a warm evening snack, this is the spot.

The must-order is the coconut milk set, 30 THB for ten pieces divided into five pandan-green and five butterfly-pea blue — the colours are entirely natural. A special larger set is available for bigger appetites. Multiple genuine reviews agree the wrappers look thick but feel surprisingly thin and soft once in your mouth, the filling is rich and intensely flavoured, and the coconut milk — fragrant but not cloying — plus crispy fried garlic on top makes everything come together perfectly. Fresh vegetables and raw chillies are provided on the side to cut through the richness. People say they get hooked every time.

The other charm is the seasonality: the cart opens only in winter, roughly from mid-October through the new year and into late February. Once the air warms it closes immediately. On weekdays it starts around 4:30 p.m., on holidays a little earlier around 4:00 p.m., and it sells until sold out — often around 8:00–8:30 p.m., sometimes earlier when the crowd is large. Come early if you want both colours, because running out is a real possibility.

A few things to know: it's a street cart with no fixed seating. Most customers buy to take home. Cash only — the vendor does not accept 1,000-THB notes. All sets are priced under 100 THB. Ratings on food review sites around 4.0, reflecting genuine quality and repeat custom year after year. If you happen to be in Nan in winter, do not miss this snack.
mustOrder: Khao krиeb pak mo with coconut milk — two-colour set
blocks.bestFor: Winter evening snack, buying to eat with the family
blocks.hours: 16:30–21:00 (winter season only, approx. mid-Oct–late Feb, closes when sold out)

blocks.name: Boklua View
blocks.signature: Phak kut fern salad, makwaen/galangal fried chicken, three-variety nam prik, fish curry, local food with valley views
blocks.descHtml:
After the winding mountain drive up to Bo Kluea Tai, when your stomach starts talking, Boklua View is the restaurant Nan locals and road-trip travellers mention most. The restaurant sits within Boklua View Resort perched on a hillside with a wide view of the green valley and the Mae Mang River stretching below. Good for couples, families, or a group on a mountain road trip — the setting delivers every time.

The dish every table orders is phak kut fern salad — wild local fern tossed in a well-rounded spicy dressing — and makwaen fried chicken or galangal fried chicken, free-range chicken fragrant with Northern spices that reviewers consistently call the standout of the menu. A three-variety nam prik platter comes assembled for dipping fresh vegetables, and fish curry — intense and hot — rounds things out. For something sweet, pumpkin baked in butter and Bo Kluea-style pork trotter are worth trying. Most ingredients are sourced from the local community, which gives the food a straightforwardly honest, home-cooked quality that isn't over-seasoned.

The dining area is a Lanna-style wooden pavilion with open-air seating cooled by mountain breezes from the valley below. A stream runs at the base of the hill and the veranda view in the afternoon is something guests say makes them forget they were even hungry. Price per person 100–250 THB, a little more when ordering a larger spread but still worth it. Open daily 11:30–20:00. Near Bo Kluea Hospital.

Worth knowing: the restaurant is roughly 85–100 km from Nan city over winding mountain roads — allow time for the drive and go slowly. During high season, calling ahead to book a table is a good idea. The space is open-air with no air conditioning, but the mountain air takes care of that. And while you're there, stop by the resort bakery — they make fresh croissants daily.
blocks.bestFor: Lunch or dinner with valley views during a Bo Kluea trip

blocks.name: Yudwela Cafe
blocks.area: Ban Sapan, Dong Phaya Sub-district, Bo Kluea District, Nan Province
blocks.signature: Coffee and drinks using local area ingredients, baked goods, sit and sip with mountain views over Ban Sapan
blocks.descHtml:
Yudwela Cafe is a hillside café in Ban Sapan village, Bo Kluea District, that many people have named the village's essential check-in spot. The building is a traditional Nan-style raised wooden house with a wide veranda facing terraced rice fields and layered mountain ridges. Come early in the morning and you stand a chance of catching sea fog drifting over the paddies. Perfect for anyone driving through Sapan who wants to sit with a coffee and a view, no hurry. It opens early while the sky is still dark, which is why sunrise and fog photographers love it.

The most ordered drinks are coffees using locally grown Nan beans — americano and latte — which reviewers describe as lightly roasted, clean-tasting, and nicely aromatic. Good for fans of brighter, fruitier profiles. The cold drink that gets mentioned most is avocado smoothie — smooth and thick — and the bakery offers coconut cake and banana cake alongside the coffees. Drink prices start around 70 THB, cakes around 85 THB, some specialty drinks up to 130 THB — fair for the view you're getting.

The view is the whole point: sitting on the veranda, you see mountains and rice fields almost 360 degrees around you. Reviews say the scenery exceeds expectations — like being transported somewhere else entirely. During the rainy season when the paddies are deep green, the setting is at its most dramatic. The high elevation means it's cool and breezy all year.

Before you go: the approach road is steep with a tight switchback near the top, so drive carefully. If the lower parking area is full, there's space near Sapan Temple further up. On long weekends the café fills quickly and the light is good for photos — arriving early gives you the best angles and shorter waits.
blocks.bestFor: Early risers wanting coffee with mountain views and sea fog at Sapan

blocks.name: Saneh Nuea
blocks.area: Mahayot Road, Nai Wiang Sub-district, Mueang Nan District, Nan Province
blocks.signature: Khao soi chicken, braised beef khao soi, crispy pork khao soi, khanom jeen nam ngiao, braised beef noodles
blocks.descHtml:
Saneh Nuea is a casual, open-air Northern Thai restaurant on Mahayot Road in the centre of Nan city, less than a five-minute drive from Nan Nakhon Airport — making it the first stop many people make right after landing. The building is an old wooden-and-tin structure hung with Lanna lanterns, plenty of seating, and easy parking nearby. Relaxed and unfussy — the kind of place you walk into as you are.

The star of the menu is khao soi, available as chicken, braised beef, or crispy pork. The curry broth is fragrant and well-bodied, the meat tender from long cooking. The other dish reviewers mention constantly is khanom jeen nam ngiao — the reviews describe it as intensely flavoured and aromatic, the kind of bowl you finish without noticing. For noodle fans there are also braised beef noodles, pork mince stir-fried with cumin over a crispy-edged fried egg, and crispy pork basil rice.

Prices are genuinely friendly — most dishes around 50–60 THB, well under 100 THB per person. Reviewers consistently call it good value. On Wongnai the restaurant scores around 4.3 from real reviewers, and it appears across multiple food pages recommending Nan restaurants. Open approximately 10:30–15:30, closed Wednesdays.

Worth knowing: the restaurant focuses on the lunch-to-afternoon period and closes fairly early, and it's shut on Wednesdays. If you're planning to go, aim for the midday slot. During tourist season there may be a queue. With the airport location and the price point, it's become one of the khao soi spots that Nan visitors tell each other about.
blocks.bestFor: First meal after landing at Nan Airport
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: khao soi · Rushen / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 2.0)

blocks.name: Krua Wan Dee Dee
blocks.cuisine: Northern Thai / Thai / À la carte
blocks.signature: Stir-fried vegetables, boldly flavoured à la carte dishes, local and Thai dishes
blocks.descHtml:
Krua Wan Dee Dee is a roadside à la carte and local food restaurant in Pua District that Nan locals and passing travellers stop at regularly. It's a single-storey open-air structure under a roof with natural ventilation and parking front and back. Good for families or groups driving around Pua who want a proper sit-down meal without bookings or long waits. The menu covers Northern Thai, central Thai, and boldly flavoured à la carte dishes — you can order a single plate or fill a whole table.

The dish ordered most and praised most in reviews is makwaen fried chicken — tender inside, crispy outside, and clearly fragrant with the Northern makwaen spice. Second is pla kang tom yum with a thick, intense broth, and phak kut fern salad — fresh and crunchy. For something local, try makwaen nam prik, or bitter melon stir-fried with egg as a milder shared plate. Most reviews agree the flavours are rich and rounded — honest home cooking done well.

Price per person approximately 101–250 THB, fair for the quality and portion size. Food comes quickly, service is warm in the Northern Thai way, and free Wi-Fi is provided. Open daily from around 09:00–21:00, so it works for both lunch and dinner. Google Maps rating 4.4 from over 100 reviews, reflecting consistent repeat visits.

Worth knowing: the sign at the front blends into the roadside and a few people say it's easy to miss — pinning the coordinates before you set out helps. During festivals or long weekends, the evening rush can be dense, but the wide parking lot and a fast kitchen keep things moving.
blocks.bestFor: First meal in Pua, family or group dining
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: northern Thai food · Jpatokal / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)

Book in advance via Klook or GetYourGuide. You leave with something to cook at home, too.

blocks.title: Before you eat your way through Nan

items.title: Getting around
items.text: Inside Nan's old town many popular spots are within walking distance of each other, but Grab is scarce. Renting a motorbike or car is recommended — especially if you're heading up to Bo Kluea and Ban Sapan, which are far out and require mountain driving.

items.title: Payment
items.text: Street food stalls, noodle shops, and seasonal snacks like khao krиeb pak mo are typically cash only. Carry small bills and coins. Sit-down restaurants and cafés often accept QR PromptPay, but international cards are not universally accepted.

items.title: Beating the queues
items.text: Mountain-view cafés like Yudwela and riverside restaurants fill up on weekend mornings and afternoons. Arriving before 10:00 gives you a comfortable seat. Khao soi spots should be visited before noon — the popular bowls sell out early.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Ordinary restaurants in Nan do not expect tips, and most don't add a service charge. Leaving the small change or 20–50 THB if you had a great meal is a nice gesture, not an obligation.

items.title: Language and menus
items.text: Many local restaurants have Thai-only menus. Picture menus help a lot. Try pointing at photos or mentioning popular dishes by name — khao soi and nam prik num are understood anywhere. Staff are generally warm and will do their best to help.

items.title: Northern Thai flavour profile
items.text: Northern Thai food is not as fiery as Isan or Southern Thai. Nam prik num and laab khua carry a mild heat. If you can't handle chilli, let the restaurant know — and consider ordering steamed vegetables with sticky rice alongside your dishes, the way locals eat.

blocks.title: How to plan eating in Nan across 1–2 days
blocks.html:
If you have one day in the city, do lunch at Saneh Nuea for khao soi or khanom jeen nam ngiao (open daytime hours, closed Wednesdays) then save dinner for Huen Phuka which stays open until around 21:00 — order the Nan appetiser platter and makwaen fried chicken to share. For a riverside atmosphere, cross to the Phu Phiang side and head to Huen Chao Nang for kaeng som pla kang and nam prik num. Huen Hom is good for a late morning stop since it's a smaller shop and the khao soi sells out.

If you're driving up toward Bo Kluea–Sapan, slot Boklua View as the lunch stop — makwaen fried chicken and phak kut fern salad with a valley view — then continue to Yudwela Cafe in Ban Sapan for coffee and the mountain panorama (hilltop cafés open early but close by late afternoon; go before it starts getting dark). On the drive back through Pua, Krua Wan Dee Dee is a solid à la carte refuel stop. Khao krиeb pak mo in front of the prison is a winter-only evening snack — if the timing lines up, grab it immediately.

faq.q: Which Nan restaurant is the most famous?
faq.a: In Nan city, Huen Phuka is one of the most talked-about names for Northern Thai food. The Nan appetiser platter and makwaen fried chicken are ordered at nearly every table. For khao soi and khanom jeen nam ngiao, locals favour Saneh Nuea. And for a riverside meal with food from the old ruling family's recipe lineage, Huen Chao Nang is equally popular.

faq.q: What signature dishes should you try in Nan?
faq.a: Northern Thai dishes worth trying in Nan include nam prik num with steamed vegetables, pork laab khua, kaeng kae gai, khao soi, khanom jeen nam ngiao, and makwaen fried chicken — the makwaen spice is unique to this region. Up in Bo Kluea, try phak kut fern salad and fish curry at Boklua View. And if you're visiting in winter, the seasonal khao krиeb pak mo in front of the prison is a local obsession.

faq.q: What does eating in Nan cost?
faq.a: Mainstream Northern Thai restaurants like Huen Phuka, Huen Hom, Huen Chao Nang, and Krua Wan Dee Dee run about 100–300 THB per person. Lung Song noodles are 40–50 THB a bowl. Khao soi at Saneh Nuea is 50–85 THB per dish. Cafés like Wevari Heritage and Yudwela Cafe are in the low hundreds. Seasonal snacks like khao krиeb pak mo are 30–50 THB a set. Overall, Nan is a good-value destination.

faq.q: Do Nan restaurants require advance booking?
faq.a: Most restaurants are walk-in. But during high season (winter) and on long weekends, popular spots in the city like Huen Phuka and riverside restaurants like Huen Chao Nang get very busy. For large groups or weekend dinners, calling ahead to reserve a table is worth it. Hilltop cafés like Yudwela don't take reservations, but arriving early avoids the crowds.

faq.q: Do Nan restaurants stay open late?
faq.a: Huen Phuka stays open until around 21:00, making it a solid dinner option. Krua Wan Dee Dee in Pua also runs into the evening. Khao soi and khanom jeen spots like Saneh Nuea focus on the daytime and close in the afternoon. Hilltop cafés like Yudwela and restaurants around Bo Kluea typically close by early evening. If you want a late dinner, staying in Nan city gives you more options.
